transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Most nights I end up eating a lot of food when I’m not even hungry, almost like I’m on autopilot after the day is over. It has really started to worry me, and I just don't know how to stop this cycle on my own.
After these episodes of eating, do you feel a strong urge to use methods like self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or laxatives to prevent weight gain?

No, I don't do any of those things at all. I have never tried to make myself throw up, take laxatives, or do extreme workouts after I eat. I just end up sitting with the discomfort and feeling really bad about it.
During these episodes, do you feel a sense of loss of control over your eating, and does it cause you significant distress or feelings of guilt afterward?

Yes, absolutely—once I start, it’s like a switch flips and I feel completely powerless to stop, even though part of my brain is telling me to. Afterward, the guilt and shame are overwhelming, to the point where I hide my eating from my family and wake up the next day feeling completely worn out.
